To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Bayesian hierarchical modeling approach is an effective means for establishing a realistic representation of causal linkages between exogenous phosphorus loading and the epilimnetic phytoplankton dynamics in Lake Simcoe.
the proposed Bayesian network can be used to identify the causal linkages among nutrient loading, water transparency, and plankton dynamics in Lake Simcoe.

the causal links between total phosphorus loading and epilimnetc plankton dynamics in Lake Simcoe can be realistically represented by a Bayesian hierarchical network that includes a mass-balance model for total phosphorus, a structural equation model for plankton, and an indicator model for water transparency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a Bayesian hierarchical network to study the causal links between total phosphorus loading and epilimnetics plankton patterns in the context of a complex ecosystem.
the application of a Bayesian hierarchical network for elucidating causal relationships between phosphorus loading, water clarity, and plankton dynamics in Lake Simcoe.

the development of an ecosystem-based modeling tool that can be used for the evaluation of the effectiveness of the nutrient loading reductions in the context of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phosphorus loading reduction is not a sufficient condition for restoring the water quality in Lake Simcoe.
the current phosphorus loading levels are still too high to allow for the attainment of the beneficial use criteria for the two embaymens of Lake Simcoe.
a 15%-20% phosphorus loading reduction will not be sufficient to meet the 4 μgL-1 chla threshold in the two embayment areas of Lake Simcoe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a reduction of the exogenous TP loading will improve water clarity in the lake, but it will not necessarily guarantee the restoration of the beneficial uses in the lake.

the Bayesian hierarchical network approach is an effective tool for the development of a mechanistic understanding of the complex interplay among the main drivers of ecosystem functioning and for the assessment of the effectiveness of management actions in restoring beneficial uses of impaired water bodies.
a Bayesian network approach can be used to elucidate the causal links among phosphorus loading, ambient nutrient concentrations, and planktonic biomass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Bayesian networks can be used to integrate and synthesize the results from multiple ecological models in an ecosystem context.

a Bayesian network of simple models can be effectively used to delineate causal links among the main components of the lake ecosystem, and to assess the potential effects of phosphorus reduction scenarios on the plankton community structure.

the use of Bayesian networks for ecosystem modeling can provide a more realistic representation of the underlying mechanisms and processes, thus facilitating the development of a more informed and effective management strategy.
